claims.text: The Q6 timing-support criteria applied to the extended spine are exactly the criteria frozen in Spec 027's Stage 0 freeze (thresholds, 5250-3850 BP window, grade and material vocabularies); this extension changes none of them.

evidence.description: Frozen Q6 timing-support criteria and thresholds
Gap table computed against the frozen criteria

alternatives: Re-freezing Q6 support with relaxed thresholds matched to the data that happen to be available.
falsification_tests: A re-test run under any threshold, window, grade rule, or material mapping differing from stage0-freeze.md section 4 and section 3.3 defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The frozen criteria were set for the Stage 0 spine and are unreasonably strict for any attainable spine, so they should be revised.
metadata.verdict_rule: Criteria identity is checked mechanically against stage0-freeze.md at freeze time; any difference is a new Spec 027 freeze, not an amendment of this spec.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C01 fixes WHICH criteria are applied; C05 fixes HOW the re-test is conducted (margins only). Changing conduct cannot change criteria without defeating C01, and C01 says nothing about conduct. C07's closure rule presumes C01: a negative outcome is only meaningful if the criteria were not loosened.

claims.text: Every chronology row the extension builds carries a complete trace: origin source, source locator, lab code, licence state, origin group, region as recorded, and scenario tag where applicable; a row missing any trace field is not built.

evidence.description: Stage 0 validators: every row carries source, licence state, origin group, grade
Extension integrity rules, rule 1 (trace or don't build)

alternatives: Admitting rows on a secondary compilation's authority with tracing deferred to a later audit.
falsification_tests: One built extension row lacking any named trace field defeats this claim.

failures.breakpoint: Claim may contain multiple independently falsifiable propositions
failures.recovery_hint: Split the claim into atomic propositions and link them explicitly.

metadata.strongest_rival: Full tracing per row is labour that duplicates the origin databases' own curation.
metadata.verdict_rule: The build's validators fail loud on any incomplete row, as Stage 0's did; the build report publishes the trace-field completeness count.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C02 requires that a row be traceable; C03 requires that traced rows not duplicate one measurement. A row can satisfy C02 and violate C03 (fully traced, but the same lab code as an existing row) - the claims govern different failure modes and neither implies the other. C06 governs what may be DONE with a traced row (release posture), not whether it is traced.

claims.text: No radiocarbon measurement is counted more than once in the extended spine or its assessment pool: measurement identity is the lab code, corroborated by age and material, across XRONOS, origin databases, aggregators, and literature extraction.

evidence.description: Dataset inventory: aggregator is not a primary source; origin database recorded per date (D5)
Extension integrity rules, rule 2 (one measurement, one row)

alternatives: Treating each route's record as an independent date because its compilation differs.
falsification_tests: Two rows in the assessment pool sharing a lab code with matching age and material, counted as independent measurements, defeat this claim.

failures.breakpoint: Claim may contain multiple independently falsifiable propositions
failures.recovery_hint: Split the claim into atomic propositions and link them explicitly.

metadata.strongest_rival: Different compilations sometimes correct a lab code or age, so strict lab-code identity could merge genuinely distinct measurements.
metadata.verdict_rule: Dedupe runs before any assessment; merges and near-miss lab-code collisions are listed in the build report with their corroboration fields, so a wrong merge is visible and reversible.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C03 presumes C02 (identity can only be checked on traced rows) but adds a distinct obligation: cross-route uniqueness. It does not govern grading (a deduplicated row still needs its own grade under the frozen rule) and does not govern C04's scenario reporting.

claims.text: Dependence on CONTESTED-scenario chronology is always visible: the re-test reports every criterion as frozen and again excluding CONTESTED-scenario rows, so no qualification silently rests on contested chronology.

evidence.description: Stage 0 report: 33 CONTESTED-scenario rows; Mehrgarh d/a status rests on them
Extension integrity rules, rule 5 (CONTESTED never silent)

alternatives: Reporting only the as-frozen computation, on the ground that the frozen criteria do not exclude contested rows.
falsification_tests: A re-test report lacking the with/without-CONTESTED line for any criterion defeats this claim.

failures.recovery_hint: Split the claim into atomic propositions and link them explicitly.

metadata.strongest_rival: The frozen criteria make no scenario exclusion, so a sensitivity report invites readers to discount a legitimately passed assessment.
metadata.verdict_rule: Both computations are published side by side with the criterion values; the claim is satisfied by the reporting, whichever way the owner later rules on bindingness.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C04 governs reporting about scenario dependence; it does not alter the criteria (C01), does not exclude any row from the pool (C02/C03 govern admission), and does not conduct the assessment (C05). Mehrgarh's contested rows are its motivating case, not its boundary.

claims.text: The re-test inspects spine margins and metadata only: no trait list is built, no first-appearance outcome is examined, and no timing model is fitted before or during the timing-support assessment.

evidence.description: Assessment from spine margins and metadata only; no trait-timing outcome inspected
Q6 support conditions must be shown before outcomes are examined

alternatives: Inspecting trait first appearances during the build to target extraction at the sites where traits appear earliest.
falsification_tests: Any trait-timing output, trait list, or fitted timing model among the extension's products defeats this claim.

failures.breakpoint: Claim may contain multiple independently falsifiable propositions
failures.recovery_hint: Split the claim into atomic propositions and link them explicitly.

metadata.strongest_rival: Outcome-guided extraction would reach testability faster by spending labour only where traits are early.
metadata.verdict_rule: Extension products are enumerated in the freeze; the assessment script's inputs are the spine products and nothing else, sha256-pinned before the run.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C05 restricts what the extension may look at; C01 restricts what it may change. Extraction targeting is ordered by criterion service on margins (site/region/material coverage), which C05 permits, and never by trait outcomes, which it forbids. C07 depends on C05: a negative closure is only honest if outcomes were never peeked at.

claims.text: Licence posture follows Spec 027 section 5.1 for every extension row, and no open_access_read_only or catalogue_only material enters any CC BY release package.

evidence.description: Licensing rule: five postures; anything not lawfully reusable is catalogued, not copied
Stage 0 release package: verified_open rows only, gate run, no deposit

alternatives: Releasing the full extended spine CC BY on the ground that radiocarbon dates are facts.
falsification_tests: One open_access_read_only or catalogue_only row in a release manifest defeats this claim.

failures.breakpoint: Claim may contain multiple independently falsifiable propositions
failures.recovery_hint: Split the claim into atomic propositions and link them explicitly.

metadata.strongest_rival: Dates are facts and facts are not copyrightable, so posture distinctions are over-caution.
metadata.verdict_rule: Release packages are built only from verified_open rows and pass the repository release gate, as Stage 0's did; posture distribution of added rows is published in the build report.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C06 presumes C02 (posture is a trace field) but governs a different act: publication. A row can be fully traced (C02 satisfied) and still barred from release (C06). It does not govern whether a permission_required source may be pursued - that is an owner decision outside this design (no-contact scope).

claims.text: A negative extension outcome - the frozen criteria still failing after all audited routes - is a valid closure that leaves Q6 NOT-YET-TESTABLE; it is never grounds to loosen a criterion, re-grade by inference, or substitute period labels for dates.

evidence.description: Registered-but-blocked discipline: unblocking is a new freeze with the changed data condition evidenced
Joint build targets and negative extension closure

alternatives: Treating a failed extension as an unfinished task to be retried with adjusted rules until Q6 becomes testable.
falsification_tests: Any criterion loosened, grade inferred, or period-label timing table offered as a substitute following a negative extension outcome defeats this claim.

failures.breakpoint: Claim may contain multiple independently falsifiable propositions
failures.recovery_hint: Split the claim into atomic propositions and link them explicitly.

metadata.strongest_rival: A program that can never make its flagship timing question testable should revise the question rather than keep reporting infrastructure.
metadata.verdict_rule: The extension's outcome record states which routes were exhausted and the remaining per-criterion gaps; Q6's status changes only via the section 6 re-test outcome, never by editorial decision.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C07 presumes C01 (criteria fixed) and C05 (outcomes unpeeked); it adds the closure rule neither contains: what may and may not be done after a negative result. Revising the Q6 QUESTION remains possible - as a new Spec 027 freeze with owner adjudication - and is not a loosening under this claim.
